skill.name: groundcover-cli
skill.description: Query Groundcover logs, traces, metrics, and Kubernetes data, and manage observability resources through documented CLI workflows.
skill.summary: Investigate production issues and manage Groundcover dashboards, monitors, and integrations with CLI guidance.
skill.author: paymog

security_audit.summary: All 244 static findings were adjudicated; three overlapping detections confirm one unverified remote-installer execution risk. Other detections concern Markdown, documented authentication, standard input, or application identifiers. No evidence found of prompt injection, covert exfiltration, or malicious intent in the supplied skill text; external implementations were not reviewed.

remediation.issue: The Grafana setup recipe executes a remotely downloaded shell installer without a pinned version or integrity check.
remediation.suggestion: Replace direct execution with a version-pinned distribution and verified signature or trusted checksum; review installer changes before execution.

content.value_statement: Production investigations require correlated logs, traces, metrics, and Kubernetes context. This skill provides Groundcover CLI workflows for querying telemetry and managing observability resources.
actual_capabilities: Provides log and trace search templates with UTC time windows and GCQL filters.
Documents PromQL range queries and metric name, label, and value discovery.
Provides Kubernetes workload and event queries for restart and warning investigations.
Explains SDK-backed resource management and raw endpoint discovery.
Documents dashboard presets, template variables, layout constraints, and revision-aware updates.
Explains keyring-backed profiles and separate Groundcover API and Grafana authentication.
limitations: Requires an installed CLI, network access, and authorized credentials; the skill contains instructions rather than a bundled executable.
Grafana commands require a separate token generated through a tenant-admin workflow.
Raw endpoints and request shapes depend on upstream APIs; some date examples require platform-specific adjustments.
Instant metric queries have documented failures, and API checks cannot fully verify dashboard appearance.

use_cases.title: Investigate Production Errors
use_cases.description: Correlate service error logs, slow traces, latency metrics, and Kubernetes warnings within a defined incident window.

use_cases.title: Validate Service Telemetry
use_cases.description: Discover available metrics and labels, then compare request latency and error patterns for an application service.

use_cases.title: Maintain Observability Dashboards
use_cases.description: Inspect dashboard presets, prepare revision-aware changes, and validate queries and layout constraints before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Check Authentication Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to check my Groundcover profile and authentication status without printing tokens. Do not install software or create credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Review Recent Service Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Using my authorized profile, inspect error logs for service api over the last hour. Summarize recurring errors without exposing sensitive log values.

prompt_templates.title: Correlate Latency and Restarts
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate api latency over the last 30 minutes using traces, PromQL range queries, and Kubernetes warnings. Separate observations from hypotheses; make no changes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Dashboard Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect dashboard <uuid> and propose p99 panels. Preserve its revision and existing widgets. Validate queries and layout; request approval before applying changes.

output_examples.input: Summarize a service incident after reviewing its telemetry.
output: Illustrative summary: Error logs show repeated upstream timeouts during the selected window.
Slow traces overlap with elevated latency metrics.
The available evidence suggests an upstream dependency issue, but does not establish the root cause.

output_examples.input: Review a proposed dashboard change before applying it.
output: Illustrative review: Preserve the current revision and existing widgets.
Place stat panels at the top level and check every panel against the 24-column grid.
Validate each metric expression with a range query.
The change remains unapplied pending approval; visual rendering has not been verified.

best_practices: Use authorized, least-privilege profiles and confirm the tenant and destination before querying or changing resources.
Use narrow UTC windows and discriminating filters; remove secrets and personal data from shared findings.
Preserve current revisions and complete settings; obtain approval before writes, alert silences, or software installation.
anti_patterns: Executing the remote installer without reviewing it and verifying a pinned artifact.
Printing API tokens or copying unredacted production logs into reports.
Silencing alerts or overwriting production dashboards without explicit approval and a recovery plan.

faq.question: Does this skill include the Groundcover executable?
faq.answer: No. It provides CLI instructions and request templates. You must install the appropriate executable separately.

faq.question: Which API key type is required?
faq.answer: Standard API workflows require a service-account key with the gcsa_ prefix. Ingestion keys do not authenticate these commands.

faq.question: Can the same key access embedded Grafana?
faq.answer: No. The documented Grafana workflows require a separate glsa_ service-account token and tenant-admin setup.

faq.question: Should I use SDK-backed or raw commands?
faq.answer: Prefer SDK-backed commands. Use raw endpoint discovery when the SDK lacks the required operation.

faq.question: Can this skill change production resources?
faq.answer: Yes, its documented commands include updates, deletions, credential creation, and alert silences. Use least privilege and require approval for changes.

faq.question: Why can an instant metric query fail?
faq.answer: The skill documents instant-query failures. Use a short range query and inspect the latest point, accounting for delayed metric ingestion.
